title: Parameterized STL geometry assets and provenance
overview: Defines how OneFLOW prepares reproducible STL surface assets for the unit sphere, 6:1 prolate spheroid and internal-flow cylinder. The geometry library records analytic identity, parameters, units, generator provenance, surface metrics and (where applicable) boundary-patch facet indices in a companion .geometry.json manifest. STL assets are surface inputs, not volume meshes or solver boundary-condition definitions.
principle: Keep analytic geometry parameters, surface discretization and Gmsh volume-mesh size independent. A generated STL is a piecewise-planar approximation of its analytic definition. Preserve asset identity and provenance with a manifest bound to the exact STL bytes. Preserve patch identity explicitly because STL has no standard Physical Group mechanism. Do not silently scale coordinates when changing unit metadata.
architecture: Geometry Library / GUI parameters -> grid/stl_to_gmsh/generate_stl_geometry.py -> STL + .geometry.json -> grid/stl_import/reader.py -> topology validation in grid/stl_import/surface.py and grid/stl_to_gmsh/converter.py -> geometry-specific Gmsh adapter -> MSH 4.1. Native C++ consumes checked-in Case assets through StlMeshReader and GridConversion.cpp. The sphere and spheroid use the generic closed-shell reconstruction path; the internal-flow cylinder uses a manifest-driven analytic OpenCASCADE cylinder path to preserve wall/inflow/outflow identities.

proves: The deterministic generator provides parameterized sphere, prolate-spheroid and internal-flow-cylinder surface construction and emits a companion provenance manifest.
The unit sphere uses an icosphere subdivision construction; the prolate spheroid reuses that connectivity and applies semi-axis scaling.
The cylinder surface is constructed from axial rings and circumferential divisions and labels wall, inflow and outflow facets separately.
The cylinder C++ and Python Cases are registered as distinct implementations sharing the analytic asset identity and patch contract.
Generated user variants are written outside the repository source tree under the OneFLOW user workspace.
Geometry discretization controls and Gmsh volume-mesh characteristic length are separate parameters.
does_not_prove: Changing the manifest unit label performs coordinate conversion; it does not.
STL contains portable Gmsh Physical Groups or CFD boundary-state data.
Every legacy checked-in sphere and spheroid fixture was emitted byte-for-byte by the current deterministic generator.
The C++ cylinder path performs the same SHA-256 verification as the Python adapter.
A watertight STL alone guarantees good element quality, physical CFD validity or grid convergence.

verification.scope: tools/test_mesh_cases.py; checks the checked-in native cylinder STL against its manifest checksum and verifies exact, non-overlapping wall/inflow/outflow facet coverage.
grid/tests/python/stl_to_gmsh/test_stl_geometry_generation.py; generator-level regression coverage for deterministic geometry and manifest output.
tools/oneflow_gui/test_mesh_generation_dialog.py; GUI geometry preset and asset selection behavior.
